patches.reason: The VIP handrail is rigid and close to the camera, and it contradicts the hair-bow-driven 0.6 m arc. Measured rail top-edge rows at x=800 are 1766 (f190), 1775 (f210) and 1779 (f220); the spec projects 2085, 1963 and 1908, so the rail is out of frame in f170-190. The prow corner, where DS's wrist rests and the rail disappears under her sleeve, projects at x=1479 at f200, but the visible rail end is at x≈780. Fix: move each location along the right-wing direction u=(0.896,-0.445,0) by s = 0.20 m (f149-176), 0.159 (f200), 0.095 (f230), 0.032 (f260) and 0.006 (f303), with targets and rolls unchanged. Result: rail median 4-5 px (max 21), corner at the visible rail end, lamps ≤9 px, fascia ≤1 px, beam unchanged, CL head blob median 5.2 / max 25.3 px. Verified in a bpy build with world_to_camera_view.

The shot-1 camera absorbed DS's sideways drift, so the sharp chrome clamp post at the prow corner drifts off its source position. Measured post neck columns: 184 (f1), 145 (f49), 81 (f73), 34 (f85). The spec projects 190, 234, 198 and 147, errors of 89, 117 and 113 px; the cheat note claims only 20-45 px. Her forearms stay about 0.10 m from the post all shot, so the set is rigid and her head is what moves. Fix: shift each key in X (location and target together) by -0.003 to -0.047 m so the post lands on its measured column, held at -0.041 m after f85. Post error drops to ≤5.7 px. Rail rows and the skyline are unchanged, since the shift is along the rail.

New extension key, documentation only. With the set-locked CAM_Shot1, DS's face point F moves by this X offset in metres (her head and upper body slide to her left, -X, while her forearms stay on the rail). With it the face boxes are reproduced at median 3.0 px / max 9.3 px. A still head would be off by about 110-155 px from f55.

New extension key. With the rail-consistent CAM_Shot2, the template-tracked hair bow pixels (810,553) f150, (632,535) f175, (433,523) f200, (240,497) f230 and (88,465) f258 back-project to these points, at the same lens distance as before (0.61-0.81 m). Over the shot her head slides about 13 cm to her left. The old static bow (-0.502,-6.692,5.344) is valid only with the old arc camera.
The rack-focus start point follows the moved bow. The focus distance is 0.61 m at f149, 0.67 m at f176 and 8.87 m to CL at f200.

findings: Overall: all three character anchors reproduce as reported. With the builder-faithful camera (euler interpolation plus hold bake) I measured shot-1 DS face 4.2/9.3 px, shot-2 CL head blob 6.2/20.4 px and shot-3 CL face 12.0/25.9 px (median/max). bpy world_to_camera_view matches. The schema is valid: 8 supported geometry types, every material exists, names are unique, and camera keys cover 1-148, 149-303 and 304-452. The cadence holds are justified: frame-to-frame differences are 0.00-0.07 for f%5==2 against 7-12 for the other frames, and 1.38 for f%5==3 in shot 1. The problems are near, rigid set elements that the cameras were bent to avoid, plus one geometry bug. All fixes are in the patches, and the patched spec builds and checks clean.

MAJOR - Shot 2 VIP handrail, f160-f250 (only f303 was checked before). The source shows the chrome rail as a diagonal at the lower right from f160 on. Fitted top-edge rows at x=800: 1766 (f190), 1775 (f210), 1779 (f220), 1787 (f250), 1785 (f260), 1774 (f280). The spec projects 2085, 1963, 1908, 1791, 1781 and 1783: the rail is out of frame for f170-f190 and 130-190 px low at f210-f220. The prow corner, where DS's right wrist rests and the rail disappears under her sleeve, projects at x=1479 at f200 and 836 at f240, against visible rail ends at ≈780 and ≈580. Cause: the 0.6 m camera arc was solved from the parallax of DS's hair bow, which belongs to a moving character. The extended wing line already passes through the measured rail, so only motion along the rail is wrong. Patch: move each location along u=(0.896,-0.445,0) by 0.20 m (f149-176) down to 0.006 m (f303), with targets unchanged. Result: rail median 4-5 px (max 21), corner at the sleeve edge, CL blob median 5.2 / max 25.3 px, lamps ≤9 px, fascia ≤1 px, beam unchanged. DS's bow then follows a track that slides about 13 cm to her left (in the patch).

MAJOR - Shot 1 clamp post at the prow corner. I tracked its chrome neck: 184 (f1), 178 (f13), 166 (f25), 145 (f49), 113 (f61), 81 (f73), 34 (f85). The spec gives 190-234, so the error is 52 px at f25, 89 px at f49 and 117 px at f73, staying above 100 px until the post leaves frame around f91. The note's '20-45 px in f1-69' understates this. DS's hands stay about 0.10 m from the post while her face moves about 4 cm toward screen-right, so the drift is hers, not the set's. The skyline at infinity moves only about -20 px. Patch: shift the camera in X by -0.003 to -0.047 m to lock the post (≤5.7 px), and carry the drift as characters.DS.shot1_face_drift_x. Face anchors with the drift: median 3.0 / max 9.3 px.

BUILDER caveat, not a spec bug: build_crowd keys bounce every period_frames//2 frames. With period 30, t advances by π per key, so variants with phase 0 or 15 never bounce (sin=0 at every key) and half the crowd is bounce-free. Any even period has the same problem. Use an odd period (29 or 31) or key every period//4.
